  3. bindgen: Odin output and Odin input

#bindgen: Odin output and Odin input

src/tools/bindgen generates every copy of the web API from one description. Historically the description was written in .widl (a small dialect of Web IDL, see docs/api/README.md) and the low-level glue the JavaScript engine links against was generated in C (native/js/gen/*). Two changes move the whole chain to Odin, so no C is written by us:

  1. -emit:odin generates the engine glue in Odin instead of C.
  2. The description itself can be written in Odin (-convert-widl migrates the existing .widl), read with a dedicated Odin reader.

The engine is Odin now, and neither of these is what the build runs: bindgen with no flag, and build.bat, read .widl and emit -emit:glue, the whole glue in Odin (native/js/odin/bindings_gen.odin). The C output (native/js/gen/*) is no longer used. What follows describes the two optional forms.

#-emit:odin : the engine glue in Odin

bindgen -emit:odin writes, instead of native/js/gen/*:

filewhatC counterpart
native/js/odin/wj/wr_imports.odin (emitted in both modes: the ported glue links against it)the browser's imports for an Odin guest: wr_* handle / enum / flags / struct / callback types and one foreign block per module with the raw ABI (@(link_name=...), the Wasm import module on foreign import)native/js/gen/wren_api.h
native/js/odin_gen/js_interfaces_table.odinthe realm's interface table: IFACE_* index constants, the member tables ([]wj.Member), and the interface table ([]wj.Interface) with names, kinds, flags, constants, [Exposed], inheritance ranges and the legacy platform-object classnative/js/gen/bindings.c + bindings.h

The generated Odin is written against native/js/odin_gen/wj_iface.odin: the Odin counterpart of the interface-table part of native/js/engine/wj.h (the types Interface, Member, the Expose / Member_Flag / Interface_Flag bit-sets, the Native / Getter / Setter glue signatures, and the conversion / wrap / throw surface the trampolines call). No macros: tagged enums, bit_set, and plain slice literals.

wj_iface.odin is stubs today: every procedure panics or returns a sentinel. It defines exactly what the generated code and the hand-written members expect, so a layer can implement it (or re-point the generated import at its package) without touching a line of the generated output. The member glue bodies (the per-member trampolines that marshal strings, bytes, handles, raises → status, [Owned]) are not generated in Odin yet: they are the part most tightly coupled to the engine's value type and conversions. The table's fn / get / set slots are left nil with the member recorded in docs/js/coverage.md; generating them is the follow-up once wj_iface.odin is backed for real.

Verify: build\bindgen.exe -emit:odin then odin check native/js/odin -vet -no-entry-point.

#The Odin description form

bindgen -convert-widl writes one .odin next to each api/*.widl (see the convention in src/tools/bindgen/idl/convert.odin and the reader src/tools/bindgen/idl/odin_in.odin). A module is one file:

Odin
//@wb module name=url order=58 exposed=(Window,Worker)
/// URL and URLSearchParams ...
package api_url

//@wb handle parent=Object host=Url_Object lookup=lookup_URL
/// A parsed absolute URL.
URL :: distinct Handle

/// A component of a URL.
URLComponent :: enum i32 { Href, Protocol, /* ... */ Origin }

//@wb flags base=u32
Opts :: enum u32 { X, Y }                      // bit numbers in order, like .widl flags

S :: struct { a: i32, kind: URLComponent, on: bool }

//@wb callback
Done :: #type proc "contextless" (user: i32, thing: Thing)

//@wb fn raises optional=base
/// new URL(input, base) ...
URL_parse :: proc(input: string, base: string = "") -> URL

Odin's own syntax carries the shape (distinct handle types, enum, struct, #type proc, proc). A //@wb directive comment carries what Odin cannot say: the module's [Exposed] and declaration order; a handle's parent, host type and lookup; a function's raises / [Owned] (owned) / [Effects] (effects) / [Exposed] / [On] / [Host], and which parameters are optional or out (named, so the proc stays a plain parameter list). /// doc comments are kept verbatim.

A module split across several .widl files (e.g. dom, declared in dom.widl and extended by ~18 partial module dom blocks) converts to several files; the directive's name= merges them back, and order= restores the original declaration order so every generated output is byte-identical.

#Why a hand-written reader, not core:odin/parser

core:odin/ast is syntactic (no resolved types — the brief's point) and drops the /// / //@wb comments unless they are collected and re-attached by position. The reader (odin_in.odin) is a small tokenizer modelled on the .widl parser (parse.odin): it keeps the docs and directives exact and makes the round-trip deterministic. It fills the same Api / Module / Decl the .widl parser does, so every downstream emitter (host, SDK, docs, conformance, imports) is untouched.

#Guardrails (read time, with file and line)

odin_in.odin rejects, by name and position:

  • a parameter or field named like an Odin keyword (context, map, proc, in, ...): the generated glue would not compile;
  • an out parameter that is not bytes (an out parameter is a host-filled buffer);
  • an enum / flags base that is not i32 / u32 (it would truncate in the ABI).

The shared check still enforces the .widl-era rules (reserved host locals c / a / f / _…, unknown types, duplicate imports, ...).

#Verifying the migration is lossless

bindgen -convert-widl then bindgen -verify-roundtrip loads both api/*.widl and the converted api/*.odin, generates the host trampolines, every guest SDK module, the docs, the conformance tests and the Odin imports from each, and reports the first byte that differs. It prints identical (host, guests, docs, conformance, imports) when the Odin form reproduces the exact output (the docs' Source: line, which names the file, is normalized away — the migration renames the source, not the API).

#What -emit:odin would need

native/js/odin_gen/wj_iface.odin is the contract. A real layer would back it with the engine-agnostic Odin layer (the wj.h equivalent): the real Ctx / Val, the to_* conversions, wrap_node / wrap_host / wrap_owned, the throw_* helpers, the scratch buffer, and it publishes interfaces / interface_count (the generated @(init) already assigns them). The member-glue body generator (the Odin equivalent of jsgen's emit_import_glue) comes once that surface is real.
